newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Copel eyes ADS launch this week.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Copel eyes ADS launch this week.

text.p: Brazilian state-owned electric company Copel said it hopes to launch this week Level Three American Depositary Shares (ADS) in New York to become the first local power firm to trade abroad.
Copel officials said the move would be part of a planned combined foreign and local offering of up to 30 billion preferred B shares to raise money for its 1997 and 1998 investment programs.
The dollar value of the issue and the amounts to be placed in the United States and Brazil had not been formally decided yet, they added.
But a local news agency said Copel planned to raise $460 million from the placement, with $372.3 million placed in the U.S. market and $87.7 million in Brazil.
"That is not confirmed yet," one official in Copel's market relations department said. "There is no public confirmation of the amount or the date."
But he added the company hoped to place the shares on Wednesday and that company officials were now in the United States on a road-show.
Copel, known formally as Companhia Paranaense de Energia SA, is owned by the southeastern Brazilian state of Parana.
A Level Three ADR or ADS program allows foreign firms to list and issue shares in the United States.
Copel preferred B rose 5.5 percent to 21.10 reais, while its common was up 2.81 percent at 20.50 reais at 1553 local/1853 GMT/1853 GMT in Sao Paulo.
